newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-DUNHILL CUP CHAMPIONS FACE NEW CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-DUNHILL CUP CHAMPIONS FACE NEW CHALLENGE.

text.p: An American trio with fresh fields to conquer move from the famous Old Course links at St Andrews to the cultured, tree-lined fairways and greens of Wentworth in southern England this week.
The World Matchplay championship is the next port of call for Mark O'Meara, Phil Mickelson and Steve Stricker following their successful assault on the Alfred Dunhill Cup at the weekend.

But even before they left Scotland they were thinking of a return in a year's time to what the Scots call the "Auld Grey Toon" now the coveted team contest has been secured for St Andrews for a further three years.

"It's a very special event and I think that playing it at St Andrews makes it that little more special," said Mickelson, whose victory over Greg Turner in the final was pivotal to the American success against New Zealand.
"I leave here hopeful that I can come back and play in it again next year," added the winner of four U.S. titles and some $1.6 million this year.
Mickelson and Steve Stricker were successful in their first bids for the title but O'Meara had not tasted success as part of the first three U.S. teams in 1985, 1986 and 1987.
"To get a victory at my fourth attempt is very gratifying," said O'Meara, the team captain.
"Phil had such a great year in the States I wanted him to be captain but we all worked together and talked a lot.

"I'm glad I could play up to a decent standard. You don't want to ley your team mates down," said O'Meara, who began with a 63 on the first day -- one shot outside the course record held by compatriot Curtis Strange.
"After that I said let's put me out first each time against their best guy. They were happy with that and I was happy to do that."
Stricker was the quiet hero of the U.S. team after winning all five of his matches in his first visit to St Andrews.
"It was an enjoyable week. These guys have been on the tour longer than I have and I am trying to raise my game to their level," he said.
Inida, playing for the first time after not being deemed worthy of an invitation before this year, certainly raised their game for the tournament.
They gave Zimbabwe a scare before losing 2-1 on the first day and then beating holders Scotland 2-1 on Saturday in one of the game's biggest upsets.
Team members Jeev Singh and Gaurav Ghei were each ranked 696th and Ali Sher did not even have a ranking.
